title: How to Make Crispy Bacon Wrapped Scallops on a Reusable Grill Mat
keyword: bacon wrapped scallops on a grill mat
meta_description: Learn how to make perfect bacon wrapped scallops on a grill mat. No sticking, no flare-ups, just crispy bacon and tender scallops every time.
html:
There is arguably no better appetizer to bridge the gap between a backyard barbecue and a fancy dinner party than bacon wrapped scallops. However, anyone who has tried to grill them knows the frustration. The bacon grease drips onto the burners causing massive flare-ups, the delicate scallops stick to the grates, and often, the small mollusks slip right through the cracks into the fire. That is why learning how to make bacon wrapped scallops on a grill mat is a total game-changer for your outdoor cooking repertoire.

Why Grill Mats Are a Game Changer for Seafood

Grilling seafood requires a delicate touch that standard metal grates often fail to provide. You need high heat to crisp the bacon, but direct exposure to flame can char the scallop before the bacon is fully cooked. This is where the BBQ Grill Mats come into play. These reusable non-stick mats create a flat, solid barrier between your food and the open flame.

p>By using a mat, you eliminate the risk of your scallops falling through the grates. More importantly, the mat acts as a heat diffuser. It allows the scallops to cook evenly in their own juices and the rendered bacon fat, rather than having all that flavor drip away into the abyss of your firebox. Because they are non-stick, you get a beautiful sear on the bacon without the need for excessive oil, and cleanup is incredibly simple since the burnt-on residue stays on the mat rather than your grill grates.

Selecting the Right Scallops and Bacon

Before you fire up the grill, the success of your dish starts at the grocery store. For the best results, you need to pay close attention to the type of scallops and the cut of bacon you are buying.

When buying scallops, look for "dry" scallops rather than "wet" scallops. Wet scallops have been treated with a phosphate solution to retain water, which prevents them from searing properly and gives them a soapy flavor. Dry scallops are natural, ivory-colored, and will caramelize beautifully on the grill. Regarding size, aim for sea scallops (often labeled U/10 or U/15), which are large enough to handle a wrap of bacon without overcooking instantly.

For the pork, standard thin-sliced bacon often burns before the scallop is cooked through. Thick-cut bacon is superior here because it takes longer to crisp, giving the scallop time to cook to a perfect, opaque doneness. If you only have thin bacon, you can partially cook it in the microwave before wrapping to speed up the process on the grill.

Preparation and Wrapping Techniques

Preparation is key to ensuring everything stays intact during the cooking process. Start by patting your scallops extremely dry with paper towels. If they are wet, they will steam on the mat rather than sear. Season them lightly with salt, pepper, and perhaps a sprinkle of garlic powder or paprika.

Wrapping can be tricky because bacon shrinks as it cooks. To prevent the wrap from unravelling, cut your bacon strips in half crosswise. Wrap a strip around the circumference of the scallop and secure it with a toothpick. Soak your wooden toothpicks in water for at least 20 minutes beforehand so they don't burn up on the grill. For a professional touch, try to tuck the loose end of the bacon strip underneath itself or the toothpick to ensure it stays tight.

How to Cook Bacon Wrapped Scallops on a Grill Mat

Now that your ingredients are prepped, it is time to grill. The mat provides a stable surface, but you still need to manage your heat correctly to get that perfect texture.

  1. Preheat the Grill: Get your grill to a medium-high heat, around 400°F. Once the grates are hot, place your BBQ Grill Mats on top. Give them a minute or two to heat up.
  2. Oil the Mat: While the mats are non-stick, a light coating of high-smoke-point oil (like canola or avocado) ensures the bacon gets extra crispy.
  3. Place the Scallops: Arrange the scallops on the mat, leaving a little space between each one so air can circulate and the bacon fat can render out.
  4. Grill Time: Close the lid. Grill for about 4-5 minutes per side. Because the mat prevents direct flame contact, you don't have to worry as much about flare-ups, but keep an eye on the bacon color.
  5. The Glaze (Optional): If you want a sticky glaze—like a maple-bourbon or chili-honey sauce—brush it on during the last 2 minutes of cooking. The sugars will caramelize on the mat without burning instantly.
  6. Check Doneness: The scallops should be opaque and firm to the touch, and the bacon should be browned and crispy. Remove them to a platter and let them rest for 2 minutes before serving.

Serving Suggestions

These scallops are best served immediately while the bacon is still snapping with crispiness. They are excellent on their own, but a dipping sauce elevates them to a restaurant-quality dish. A lemon-garlic butter sauce is a classic choice that cuts through the richness of the pork. If you prefer something with a kick, a spicy sriracha mayo or a sweet and sour chili sauce works wonderfully.

Garnish the platter with fresh chopped parsley or chives to add a pop of color that contrasts the golden-brown bacon. Because you cooked on a reusable mat, you can serve these knowing they didn't pick up any gritty residue from a dirty grill grate, keeping the presentation pristine.

FAQ

Do I need to flip the scallops when using a grill mat?

Yes, you should flip them. While the heat distributes well on a mat, the bacon needs direct contact with the hot surface on both sides to render the fat and become evenly crispy.

Can I use frozen scallops for this recipe?

You can, but you must thaw them completely first. It is vital to pat them very dry with paper towels after thawing to remove excess moisture, otherwise, they will steam on the mat rather than sear.

How do I clean the grill mat after cooking grease-heavy bacon?

Once the mats have cooled completely, wash them in warm soapy water with a soft sponge or cloth. The non-stick surface usually releases the bacon grease easily, but avoid using abrasive scouring pads or steel wool as they can damage the mat's coating.
